paper_title: Good r-Divisions Imply Optimal Amortized Decremental Biconnectivity
classifications: Theory of computation → Dynamic graph algorithms
statement: Finally, since the total number of edges in a minor-free graph is O(n), the data structure above has the optimal amortized update time for edge deletions and vertex deletions, both. The question of whether our data structure generally admits vertex deletions in O(n) total time remains open.
context: ▶ Theorem 24. Given a graph G with n vertices that does not have a Kℓ -minor, and any t(n) ∈ O(poly(log n)) we can compute a t-suitable pair of r-divisions in O(n) time. Finally, since the total number of edges in a minor-free graph is O(n), the data structure above has the optimal amortized update time for edge deletions and vertex deletions, both. The question of whether our data structure generally admits vertex deletions in O(n) total time remains open.
